method: Tests transpile and execute the exact controller copied into the disposable app using deterministic Window/event/timer doubles; no browser actions or actual credential traffic.
cases: construction and elapsed idle time never send or install listeners
a queued old timeout cannot overwrite the second attempt
waiting exposes monotonic elapsed time and send return
only tagged ready messages are observed; trusted auth reply is recorded without a token value
wrong-source and wrong-origin auth do not complete the attempt
a sender exception is explicit and cancels the timer and listeners
missing and closed opener are distinguished without a send
a reply during the React subscriber gap survives and is shown on remount
completed reply metadata survives a component remount without replaying the handshake
timeout cleans every message, pagehide and timer resource even without a subscriber
StrictMode-style unsubscribe/resubscribe and module re-evaluation reuse one target controller
a controller copied onto another target is not reused for that window
real document pagehide interrupts active work without sending or waiting for React
closed opener and closed target clean active work on the bounded ticker
a prematurely invoked current timer is labeled TIMER_EARLY instead of a five-second timeout
change: Per-rendered-window singleton owns the manual attempt across React remounts; React owns only unsubscribeable UI bindings. Reply/deadline/repeat/document lifecycle cleans event/timer resources.
review: Dedicated devil reviewer independently reran all15 tests and returned SHIP for manual observation.
limitations: No live debug-tab auth reply is claimed by these unit tests.
Product auth replies do not echo an attempt id; observations use active attempt, sender/origin and timing.
No automatic sends or replay; sending occurs only from the user button click.
